analysis.detail: Netty SslHandler resource exhaustion vulnerability via SSLEngine. This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious SSL/TLS data to a Netty server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run a TLS server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections.

vulnerabilities.description: An attacker can bypass IPv6 subnet rules due to an incorrect masking operation in IpSubnetFilterRule.compareTo(). Valid public IP addresses can bypass the restrictions. The io.netty.handler.ipfilter.IpSubnetFilterRule#compareTo(java.net.InetSocketAddress) method performs a bitwise AND between the incoming IP address and the configured networkAddress, instead of the subnetMask.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not import or configure Netty IpSubnetFilter access-control rules.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable IpSubnetFilterRule access-control path is not imported or configured by Liquibase.

analysis.detail: Netty IpSubnetFilterRule IPv6 subnet filtering vulnerability fixed in 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final. Liquibase dependency management includes Netty versions below the fixed releases (pom.xml:116, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-extension/pom.xml:65, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:308, commercial-databases/liquibase-commercial-bigquery/pom.xml:73, commercial-databases/liquibase-cassandra/pom.xml:60, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-deps/pom.xml:51), so this assessment does not rely on a version-fixed claim. The vulnerable access-control API is not reachable: a focused grep for IpSubnetFilterRule, io.netty.handler.ipfilter, RuleBasedIpFilter, UniqueIpFilter, and IpFilterRule across Java and XML sources returned zero hits.

vulnerabilities.description: SslClientHelloHandler.decode() reads the 24-bit TLS handshake length and, when the ClientHello does not fit in the first record, eagerly allocates ctx.alloc().buffer(handshakeLength). Common SniHandler and AbstractSniHandler constructors can disable the length guard and timeout, allowing a 16 MiB request to cause immediate huge or unpooled allocation retained until the channel closes.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not import or configure Netty SNI handlers or TLS ClientHello server-side processing.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable Netty SNI and TLS ClientHello server-side path is not imported or configured by Liquibase.

analysis.detail: Netty SslClientHelloHandler/SniHandler allocation vulnerability fixed in 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final. Liquibase dependency management includes Netty versions below the fixed releases (pom.xml:116, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-extension/pom.xml:65, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:308, commercial-databases/liquibase-commercial-bigquery/pom.xml:73, commercial-databases/liquibase-cassandra/pom.xml:60, cloud-integrations/liquibase-azure-deps/pom.xml:51), so this assessment does not rely on a version-fixed claim. The vulnerable server-side SNI path is not reachable: a focused grep for SniHandler, AbstractSniHandler, SslClientHelloHandler, netty.handler.ssl.Sni, ClientHello, SNIMatcher, and SNIHostName across Java and XML sources returned zero hits.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. Prior to versions 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final, SimpleTrustManagerFactory.engineGetTrustManagers() and related paths wrap any user-supplied plain X509TrustManager in X509TrustManagerWrapper, which extends X509ExtendedTrustManager but implements the 3-arg checkServerTrusted(chain, authType, SSLEngine) by discarding the SSLEngine and calling the 2-arg delegate. Because the object now IS an X509ExtendedTrustManager, neither SunJSSE's internal AbstractTrustManagerWrapper nor Netty's own OpenSslX509TrustManagerWrapper will re-wrap it to add endpoint-identification. Consequently, even though Netty 4.2 sets endpointIdentificationAlgorithm="HTTPS" by default, a client built with `SslContextBuilder.forClient().trustManager(somePlainX509TrustManager)` performs no hostname verification at all. Versions 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final patch the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not construct Netty client SSL contexts with a plain X509TrustManager, and current source imports patched Netty BOM versions.

ratings.justification: Liquibase Secure does not call the Netty SSL builder or custom X509TrustManager APIs required to trigger this hostname verification bypass, so the vulnerable path is not reachable from application code.

analysis.detail: Netty hostname verification can be bypassed when client code passes a plain X509TrustManager through SslContextBuilder.forClient().trustManager(...). The scanner reported io.netty:netty-handler 4.1.133.Final, which is listed in the commercial distribution license metadata (core/liquibase-dist/src/main/archive/licenses/commercial/README.txt:526), but the source build now imports the patched Netty 4.1.135.Final BOM (pom.xml:114, pom.xml:116) and the liquibase-checks module imports the patched Netty 4.2.15.Final BOM (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:306, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:308). The vulnerable code path is not reachable from Liquibase code: focused greps across Java sources for SslContextBuilder, SimpleTrustManagerFactory, trustManager(, and X509TrustManager returned zero hits.
